t2489.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Salama ibn Dīnār, Abū Ḥāzim al-Aʿraj al-Afzar al-Tammār al-Madanī al-Qāṣṣ, client of al-Aswad ibn Sufyān, as trustworthy and devout, of the fifth generation; he died during al-Manṣūr's caliphate.
as: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
He was trustworthy and transmitted many hadiths.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
محمد بن إسحاق بن خزيمة, quoted by al-Mizzī
محمد بن إسحاق بن خزيمة, quoted by al-Mizzī
There was no one like him in his time.
لابن أبو حازم, quoted by al-Mizzī
من حدثك إن أبي سمع من أحد من الصحابة غير سهل بن سعد فقد كذب
Whoever tells you that my father heard any Companion other than Sahl ibn Saʿd has lied.
كان أبو حازم جاري، وما ظننت أنه يحسن مثل هذه الكلمات.
Abū Ḥāzim was my neighbour, and I did not expect him to be capable of words like these.
He was trustworthy and transmitted many hadiths.

as: Originally Kufan, he lived at al-ʿAskar and was reliable.
مديني الأصل، كوفي الدار، ورد بغداد، وحدث بها وبسر من رأى، وكان ثقة.

t4616.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records ʿAṭiyya ibn Saʿd ibn Junāda al-ʿAwfī al-Jadalī al-Kūfī, Abū al-Ḥasan, as truthful but frequently mistaken, a Shiʿi who practiced tadlīs, of the third generation, who died in the year 11 (after 100).
as: صدوق يخطىء كثيرا وكان شيعيا مدلسا
Truthful but makes many mistakes; he was a Shiʿi and practiced tadlīs.
عطية، وأبو هارون، وبشر بن حرب عندي سواء
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd: ʿAṭiyyah, Abū Hārūn and Bishr ibn Ḥarb are the same to me (all weak).
بلغني أن عطية كان يأتي الكلبي ويسأله عن التفسير وكان يكنيه بأبي سعيد فيقول: قال أبو سعيد
He would ask al-Kalbī about exegesis and call him Abū Saʿīd, then say 'Abū Saʿīd said' (a misleading tadlīs).
كان الثوري وهشيم يضعفان حديث عطية
Al-Thawrī and Hushaym considered ʿAṭiyyah's hadith weak.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
ضعيف، يكتب حديثه، وأبو نضرة أحب إلي منه
Weak; his hadith is written; Abū Naḍrah is dearer to me than him.
إبراهيم بن يعقوب الجوزجاني, quoted by al-Mizzī
وهو مع ضعفه يكتب حديثه، وكان يعد مع شيعة أهل الكوفة
Despite his weakness his hadith is written; he was counted among the Shīʿah of Kufa.
كان الثوري وهشيم يضعفان حديث عطية
وكان ثقة إن شاء الله وله أحاديث صالحة. ومن الناس من لا يحتج به
He was reliable, God willing, with sound hadiths; some people do not use him as proof.

t7309.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Hisham ibn Yusuf al-San'ani, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman the judge, as trustworthy, from the ninth generation. He died in 97 AH.
as: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
لم يكن به بأس، كان هو أضبط عن ابن جريج من عبد الرزاق.
There was no objection to him. He was more accurate than ʿAbd al-Razzāq in transmitting from Ibn Jurayj.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
هشام بن يوسف أثبت من عبد الرزاق في حديث ابن جريج، وكان أقرأ لكتب ابن جريج من عبد الرزاق، وكان أعلم بحديث سفيان من عبد الرزاق، وهو ثقة
Hishām was more precise in Ibn Jurayj’s hadith and read his books more proficiently than ʿAbd al-Razzāq. He knew Sufyān’s hadith better than ʿAbd al-Razzāq and was reliable.
إن حدثكم القاضي، يعني هشام بن يوسف - فلا عليكم أن لا تكتبوا عن غيره.
If the judge, meaning Hishām ibn Yūsuf, narrates to you, you need not write from anyone else.
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان هشام أصحهم كتابا من اليمانيين.
Hishām had the soundest written record among the Yemenis being compared.
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Hishām was the eldest, the best at writing, and the most precise of them.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Ibn Ḥibbān included him in The Reliable Transmitters.

t791.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Bayān ibn ʿAmr al-Bukhārī, Abū Muḥammad the devout, as truthful and eminent (ṣadūq jalīl), of the eleventh generation, who died in 22 AH.

t7950.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū Ayyūb al-Shāmī, who transmitted from al-Zuhrī, as unknown, of the seventh generation.

t8137.bio: Ibn Ḥajar lists Abū Sufyān, who transmits from ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, as acceptable (maqbūl) and belonging to the sixth generation.

t8393.bio: Ibn Ḥajar says Abū al-Mundhir was a Successor of the second generation who transmitted a mursal hadith, and some listed him among the Companions.

t8465.bio: Ibn Abī al-Ḥakam al-Ghifārī: name given as al-Ḥasan or ʿAbd al-Kabīr; obscure, of the sixth generation; Abū Dāwūd and Ibn Mājah cite him.

t8519.bio: Ibn Ḥajar lists Muṭayr, father of Sulaym, who transmits from an unnamed man identified as Dhū al-Zawāʾid, reporting from one who heard the Prophet.

t8667.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Qaylah Umm Banī Anmār, also said to be the sister of Banī Anmār, as a female Companion with a hadith on sales.

t975.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Jundub ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sufyān al-Bajalī al-ʿAlaqī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh, as having Companionship; he died after the sixtieth year.
